contracts.prefix: shared staged budget handling preserves completed indexed/local records, including explicit sorting
contracts.headings: file boundaries honor heading and filename flags in finite and unlimited ranking
contracts.preparations: source V4 uses 16 handles, 1024 eight-way 4 KiB buckets; live records pack within bounded logical pages; 32 MiB + 64 KiB directories, larger V3 and retained legacy files additional
contracts.migration: validated V2/V3 promote only on normal reads; cached-only never writes
contracts.coalescing: multiple file workers, underfilled region/line/target requests, unlimited request and region budgets; default 1 ms gather window, 0 disables, maximum 1000 ms; per-request batch-size maximum 128
contracts.scopes: cache reads/writes remain on originating client; only same options/stage/question/limits combine; wire IDs unique within a merged request
contracts.reliability: shared counters count each provider call once; retries, 413 splitting, cached-only rebatching and cancellation tested
contracts.discovery: dedicated client shares caches/model/limits and merges counters after workers join; publication mutex never spans provider I/O
contracts.large_preparations: Normal warm V3 reads do not re-encode/rewrite; regression checks exact bytes and mtime

limitations: Warm synthetic macOS fixtures on one shared host; no independent-hardware or cold-cache throughput claim
Cold microbatch fixture has two provider lanes and 20 ms latency per request; no model quality or billed-token savings established
Fewer cache files and lower CPU/RAM trade against more allocated disk on this filesystem; single-file startup is slightly slower
Linux correctness is in a VM; Windows runtime unqualified
Existing real-server scenarios were not rerun in this follow-up
Full upstream PCRE2/JIT and exhaustive ripgrep behavior remain unproven
